verses.1: And he also saw a person who was blind from birth.
verses.2: And his disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who has sinned, this man or his parents, that he should become blind?”
verses.3: Jesus replied, “Neither he nor his parents were wrong. It was so that the works of God could be revealed in him.”
verses.4: We must carry out the tasks that have been assigned to us until tomorrow. Night falls when no one is able to continue working.
verses.5: When I am in this world, I am the light of the world.
verses.6: While saying these things, he also created a kind of plaster from the mixture. He then applied that plaster to his eyes.
verses.7: And he said to him, “Go up the hillside to the pool of Siloam.” So he went up the hill, and came down to see.
verses.8: So, those who were his neighbors and those who observed him said that he was a person who always waited for others to act first. But isn’t this man the same person who always waited for others to do things first?
verses.9: Others said that it was him. Others said no, but that he was similar to him. That man said, “I am it.”
verses.10: I said to him, “How did your eyes get damaged?”
verses.11: He said this: The man who was called Jesus made a pot of clay, and he put my eyes in it. He told me to go to the hill and climb up there. So, after I went there and climbed up, I looked around.
verses.12: And they said to him, “Where is he?” He replied, “I don’t know.”
verses.13: They bring him before the Pharisees, so that they can see if he is blind.
verses.14: On the Sabbath day, Jesus created the eye, and he also removed the eyes from it.
verses.15: Once again, the Pharisees asked him how he could see clearly. He replied to them, “Pilate has put a block in my eyes. But I still can see.”
verses.16: Some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not of God, for he does not keep the Sabbath.” Others said, “How can a sinner do such things? There must be some reason for this behavior.”
verses.17: They said to the blind man again, “What do you say about him? That he has taken away your eyes.” But he replied that he was a prophet.
verses.18: Therefore, the Jews did not believe that he was blind or that he had refused to look. They continued to refuse until they told his parents to look again.
verses.19: And they asked them, “Who is this son of yours, whom you say was born blind? How can he see now?”
verses.20: So his parents replied, “We know that he is our son, and that he was born blind.”
verses.21: Now we don’t know how he sees things. We also don’t know who drew his eyes. You asked him about his age; he will talk about himself.
verses.22: These words were said by his parents, because they were afraid of the Jews. After all, the Jews had already made sure that if anyone admitted that he was the Christ, then he would be expelled from the community.
verses.23: Therefore, his parents said that he had Hylia as his wife; they married him.
verses.24: So, they praised that man, who was blind. They said to him, “May God bless him! We know that this man is a sinner.”
verses.25: So, he replied: “I don’t know if he’s a sinner. What I do know is that he’s blind when it comes to seeing things clearly.”
verses.26: I said to him, “What have you done? How have you opened your eyes?”
verses.27: He replied to them. “I have already told you, and you still haven’t heard. What do you want to hear again? Don’t you also want to become his disciples?”
verses.28: They questioned him and said, “You are a disciple of him. But we, the disciples of Moses, are indeed his true disciples.”
verses.29: We knew that Moses spoke to God, but we did not know where he came from.
verses.30: The man replied to them, “In this case, it’s amazing that you don’t know where they come from. It’s as if they have opened my eyes.”
verses.31: We know that God does not listen to the wicked. Instead, He listens only when someone who fears God acts according to His will.
verses.32: During the summer, no one heard that someone had lost their eyes due to birth defects.
verses.33: If he had not been with God, he would not have been able to do anything at all.
verses.34: They also said to him, “You were born into sin. And yet, you try to teach us?” Then they drove him out of there.
verses.35: Jesus heard that they had cast him out. When he found him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”
verses.36: He replied, “And who is he, sir, that I should believe in him?”
verses.37: Jesus said to him, “And when you see him, and he is speaking with you, then you will know that he is the one.”
verses.38: He said, “I believe, sir.” And he bowed down to him.
verses.39: And Jesus said, “I have come into this world for judgment. So that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”
verses.40: The people who were with him heard these words, and they said to him, “Aren’t we also blind?”
verses.41: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, how could you sin? But now you say, ‘Let us see.’ My sin remains with me.”
